answer: Action-trace watermarking gives each identity a salted nonce chain whose hashes spiral through every submitted action. The ledger compares chain prefixes; matching hashes expose a clone, and disputed logs move into a cold haven until an independent history arrives. A new identity costs one fresh 128-bit seed and about two CPU-hours of unique transcript, so copying pays that repeatedly and still leaves overlap. The registration inlet rejects any first ten hashes that match an existing chain.
